# ClawsGO Science

BitMiracle AI· ClawsGO Science: Cloud AI Research Agent That Runs Analyses and Drafts Cited LaTeX Papers

Open ClawsGO Science

ClawsGO Science is a hosted AI research agent from BitMiracle AI that takes a research task, works on its own cloud Linux host for hours, and delivers files such as literature reviews, analysis code, figures and LaTeX manuscripts. It suits researchers, analysts and labs who want to hand off a long literature, data-analysis or drafting job and come back to a finished deliverable.

CategoryResearch [...] ## Frequently asked questions

What is ClawsGO Science?

ClawsGO Science is a cloud AI research agent from BitMiracle AI. You describe a research task, attach any material, and an agent works on its own cloud Linux host, searching academic sources and the web, reading papers, writing and running code, and drafting documents. It delivers files such as reports, datasets, figures and LaTeX manuscripts that you can preview and edit in the app.

How much does ClawsGO Science cost? [...] ClawsGO Sciencevs.Manus

Manus is a general-purpose cloud agent for tasks such as research briefs, data collection and slide decks. ClawsGO Science uses a similar cloud-host model but is built around research work, with academic search, a LaTeX workbench, scientific file previews and SSH access to lab GPUs.

ClawsGO Sciencevs.Elicit

Elicit specializes in searching and screening scientific papers, extracting data into tables and producing cited research reports, with a dedicated systematic-review workflow. ClawsGO Science can also run literature reviews, but it executes code and analyses on its own host and drafts full manuscripts, so it covers more of the workflow while giving less structured screening and extraction tooling.

# ClawsGO Science: An AI Research Agent with a Built-in Cloud Lab

ClawsGO Science autonomously handles literature search, data analysis, code execution, and paper drafting in the cloud, with support for LaTeX compilation, scientific plotting, and connecting to lab GPUs.
